To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the size dependence of the contact angles of water droplets can be attributed to two effects: (i) the Tolman correction and (ii) a generalized line tension with contact angle dependence.

the line tension is a special case of a more general effect that depends on the droplet shape, that the line tension and the Tolman correction are comparable in magnitude, and that the size-dependent contact angle can be significant even on hydrophobic surfaces.

(i) the contact angle of water nanodrops on hydrophilic substrates is larger than the contact angle of macroscopic droplets, and (ii) the contact angle on hydrophobic substrates is smaller than the contact angle on macroscopic droplets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the Tolman correction and a generalized line tension on the contact angle of a water nanodroplet residing on a polar substrate.
the size-dependent contact angle of water nanodrops on hydrophilic and hydrophobic surfaces.
the effect of the droplet size on the contact angle, a phenomenon that is not accounted for in the standard line tension theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
line tension is a major factor that governs the contact angle of nanodroplets, but it is not the only one.
line tension is not the only effect that determines the contact angle dependence on droplet size.
the contact angle is a function of the line tension, the droplet size, and the surface polarity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for a given surface polarity, the contact angle of a nanoscopic water droplet is a function of the droplet size with a maximum at some optimal size, and the contact angle is larger for smaller droplets.
the contact angle of a nanoscopic liquid droplet on a flat surface can deviate from the macroscopic value by up to several degrees, and the effect is stronger on a hydrophilic substrate.
, in the nanoscale, the contact angle is not only a property of a droplet, but also a function of its size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the size dependence of the contact angles of nanoscopic droplets is much richer than previously assumed, and the contact angle is not a universal property, as is often assumed.
the contact angle of nanodroplets can be size-dependent even in the absence of the line tension.
the line tension is a rather coarse approximation of the contact angle dependence on droplet size, and the full description requires a more sophisticated model.
